 Celtics fans should be excited about Chris Cenac Jr.'s potential 
 Boston's got a fun prospect. By Jeff Szymanski | Nov 16, 2026, 7:03 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Boston Celtics forward Chris Cenac Jr. (12). | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Celtics picked up another win last night, crushing the Dallas Mavericks,131-94, and improving to 11-2 on the season. Jayson Tatum led the way, finishing with 32 points, 6 rebounds, and 6 assists. Given the Celtics' big lead over Dallas, we got an extended look at some end-of-rotation players in the fourth quarter, including this past year's first-round draft pick Chris Cenac Jr.
--> The Boston Celtics picked up another win last night, crushing the Dallas Mavericks,131-94, and improving to 11-2 on the season. Jayson Tatum led the way, finishing with 32 points, 6 rebounds, and 6 assists. Given the Celtics' big lead over Dallas, we got an extended look at some end-of-rotation players in the fourth quarter, including this past year's first-round draft pick Chris Cenac Jr.
 Boston selected the 6'11 big man with the 27th pick in the NBA draft following his rookie season playing for the Houston Cougars. In his lone season at Houston, Cenac averaged 9.5 points and 7.5 rebounds.
--> Boston selected the 6'11 big man with the 27th pick in the NBA draft following his rookie season playing for the Houston Cougars. In his lone season at Houston, Cenac averaged 9.5 points and 7.5 rebounds.
 Coming into the season, it was unlikely that Cenac would have a role with the Celtics, given the team's depth in the frontcourt, with Neemias Queta, Mitchell Robinson, and Luka Garza all seeing the court so far this year. Most of the time, we'll see Cenac this year be like last night, when a game is out of reach, or when he's playing for the Maine Celtics in the NBA G League. Still, watching Cenac last night showed why he is a promising prospect.

Most of the time, we'll see Cenac this year be like last night, when a game is out of reach, or when he's playing for the Maine Celtics in the NBA G League. Still, watching Cenac last night showed why he is a promising prospect.
 What makes Chris Cenac a great prospect
--> What makes Chris Cenac a great prospect
 When watching Cenac, the biggest thing that stands out is his athleticism. In the fourth quarter against the Mavs, Cenac had multiple dunks that showed off how impressive an athlete he is. You can also see his athleticism translate when he's on the defensive end of the court.
--> When watching Cenac, the biggest thing that stands out is his athleticism. In the fourth quarter against the Mavs, Cenac had multiple dunks that showed off how impressive an athlete he is. You can also see his athleticism translate when he's on the defensive end of the court.
 Currently, the Houston alum is much further along defensively than he is offensively. His biggest strength from college was his rebounding, and so far we've seen it translate during the games he's played in the G League. In his first three games for Maine, Cenac is averaging 9.7 rebounds, showing his hustle fighting for the ball.
--> Currently, the Houston alum is much further along defensively than he is offensively. His biggest strength from college was his rebounding, and so far we've seen it translate during the games he's played in the G League. In his first three games for Maine, Cenac is averaging 9.7 rebounds, showing his hustle fighting for the ball.
 During the draft process, one thing that was something to monitor was the lack of blocks that Cenac had during his time in college. As a big, you'd expect him to average a good number of blocks per game, but Cenac only averaged 0.5. So far in the G League, Cenac is showing why that concern was overblown. 
--> During the draft process, one thing that was something to monitor was the lack of blocks that Cenac had during his time in college. As a big, you'd expect him to average a good number of blocks per game, but Cenac only averaged 0.5. So far in the G League, Cenac is showing why that concern was overblown. 
 In his three games so far, Cenac is averaging 1.7 blocks per game. While some were concerned about the low block number in college, it was in part due to the defensive scheme in Houston, which saw Cenac put a bigger emphasis on rebounds over blocking shots.
--> In his three games so far, Cenac is averaging 1.7 blocks per game. While some were concerned about the low block number in college, it was in part due to the defensive scheme in Houston, which saw Cenac put a bigger emphasis on rebounds over blocking shots.
 His other question mark was his offensive abilities. Though he's able to throw down some strong dunks, his shooting still needs improvement. It hasn't been great to start the G-League season, with Cenac shooting 37.8% from the field and 20% from three. A reason to be optimistic is how Boston has helped players improve as shooters(Look at Queta starting to shoot threes at a low volume right now).

 Chris Cenac got a co-sign from Jayson Tatum
--> Chris Cenac got a co-sign from Jayson Tatum
 How he develops offensively will determine what role best suits him going forward. If he can become a better offensive player and stretch the floor, he can play either as the power forward or center, giving Boston the ability to pair him with someone like Queta on the floor. If he can't develop a shot, then he'll mostly be the center when on the court, unless paired with a stretch-five.

 If I haven't sold you on Cenac just yet, Tatum himself sees the potential with Cenac and knows he'll be a great player someday. Postgame, after beating the Mavs, Tatum talked about the Celtics' depth and how it's a strength of the roster and specifically highlighted Cenac. When discussing Cenac, Tatum stated that "Chris is gonna be good. Chris is good. But he’s really, really gonna be good. "
